_comment: Indian trading costs. Statutory charges are set by the government, the exchanges and SEBI; brokerage is set by each broker and changes often. RATES CHANGE - treat this as the structure of what you pay, and confirm the numbers with your broker before relying on them. Edit this file freely; the site reads it directly.
verify_note: Statutory rates are revised in most Union Budgets and by the exchanges. Brokerage is revised whenever a broker chooses. Always check the current rate card.

statutory.name: STT (Securities Transaction Tax)
statutory.note: The single biggest statutory cost on delivery trades. It is charged on the traded value, not on your profit.

statutory.name: Exchange transaction charges
statutory.note: Small, but it applies to the full turnover, so it matters to anyone trading frequently.

statutory.name: GST
rates: on brokerage + exchange charges + SEBI fee + DP charges
statutory.note: GST is charged on the costs, not on the trade value. It is why a 'free delivery' broker still costs you something.

statutory.name: SEBI turnover fee
statutory.note: Trivial per trade, but it exists, and it is the regulator's funding.

statutory.name: Stamp duty
statutory.note: Charged only when you buy, not when you sell. Introduced in 2020, replacing the old securities transaction tax on the buy side.

statutory.name: DP charges
statutory.when: When you sell from your demat
rates: varies by broker; commonly about ₹13.5 + GST
statutory.note: Only on delivery sells. If you sell 10 different shares in one day, that is 10 separate DP charges - which is why small holdings are expensive to exit.

statutory.name: AMC / account charges
rates: most discount brokers now charge nothing
statutory.note: Ask whether it is waived, and what happens if your holding value falls below a threshold.

brokers.name: Zerodha
brokers.note: The largest discount broker in India. Delivery is genuinely free of brokerage.

brokers.name: Groww
brokers.note: Simple app-first interface; a small number of stocks still carry a delivery charge.

brokers.name: Upstox
brokers.note: Similar structure to the others in this group.

brokers.name: 5paisa
brokers.note: Flat fee even on delivery, unlike most discount brokers.

brokers.name: ICICI Direct
brokers.note: Full-service pricing. You pay for research, relationship management and branch support.

brokers.name: Kotak Securities
brokers.note: Full-service pricing, with a discount plan available on request.

worked_example.title: What a delivery trade actually costs
worked_example.setup: Buy 100 shares at ₹1,000 and sell them at ₹1,050. Turnover ₹1,00,000 on the buy, ₹1,05,000 on the sell.
worked_example.assumption: Discount broker with nil delivery brokerage, DP charge ₹13.5 + GST.
worked_example.lesson: Costs took roughly 5% of the gross profit here. On a 1% move instead of 5%, the same trade would be barely profitable after STT and stamp duty - which is the real reason overtrading destroys returns. This hub's own backtests charge 5 basis points per side for exactly this reason.

lessons: STT is on turnover, not profit
A trade that makes no money still pays STT. Two trades that cancel each other out still cost you twice.
Which means the buy side is slightly more expensive than the sell side on delivery.
They are per scrip, per day. Ten small positions cost ten times as much to exit as one large one.
So 'zero brokerage' still carries GST on exchange charges and DP fees.
On a ₹1,00,000 delivery buy, 0.5% brokerage is ₹500 versus ₹0. Over a year of trading that difference usually dwarfs any research benefit.
Options buyers pay STT on premium
Plus the spread and time decay. It is why most option buyers lose even when they are right on direction.
